subject: Chemistry
title: Buffer Solutions & The Henderson-Hasselbalch Equation
quickSummary: Buffers resist pH change. Acidic buffer: pH = pK_a + log([Salt]/[Acid]). Basic buffer: pOH = pK_b + log([Salt]/[Base]). Maximum buffer capacity occurs at pH = pK_a with an effective range of pK_a ± 1.
summary: Master buffer classifications, Henderson-Hasselbalch equations, buffer capacity, and operational buffer ranges.

summaryBox.title: Buffer Solutions
summaryBox.takeaway: Acidic: Weak Acid + Salt with SB. Basic: Weak Base + Salt with SA. Resists pH change.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
BUFFER SOLUTION CLASSES
                                      │
         ┌────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                         ▼
   ACIDIC BUFFERS                                            BASIC BUFFERS
   Weak Acid + Its Salt with Strong Base                      Weak Base + Its Salt with Strong Acid
   (e.g., CH₃COOH + CH₃COONa)                                (e.g., NH₄OH + NH₄Cl)
conceptBreakdown.content: A Buffer Solution is a solution that resists drastic changes in $\text{pH}$ upon the addition of small amounts of strong acid or strong base, or upon dilution.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 7.2 The Henderson-Hasselbalch Equations & Buffer Capacity
conceptBreakdown.title: 7.2 The Henderson-Hasselbalch Equations & Buffer Capacity
conceptBreakdown.content:
1. **For Acidic Buffers**:
$$\mathbf{\text{pH} = \text{p}K_a + \log_{10} \left( \frac{[\text{Conjugate Base / Salt}]}{[\text{Weak Acid}]} \right)}$$

2. **For Basic Buffers**:
$$\mathbf{\text{pOH} = \text{p}K_b + \log_{10} \left( \frac{[\text{Conjugate Acid / Salt}]}{[\text{Weak Base}]} \right)} \quad \implies \quad \mathbf{\text{pH} = \text{p}K_w - \text{pOH}}$$

• **Maximum Buffer Capacity Condition**: A buffer exhibits maximum resistance to $\text{pH}$ change when $[\text{Salt}] = [\text{Acid}]$ (or $[\text{Base}]$):
$$\mathbf{\text{pH}_{\text{max capacity}} = \text{p}K_a \quad \text{and} \quad \text{Effective Buffer Range } = \mathbf{\text{p}K_a \pm 1}}$$

quickRevision: Max buffer capacity at pH = pK_a.
Buffer pH is invariant to moderate dilution.
